title: UNITE: A Unified Framework for Accurate and Efficient Origin-Destination and Route Travel Time Estimation

problem.claim: Travel time estimation on road networks includes estimating travel time between an origin and destination at a given departure time and estimating travel time along a specified route.

gap.claim: Existing approaches typically address origin-destination and route travel time estimation separately.

contributions.claim: UNITE is a unified framework that addresses origin-destination and route travel time estimation with a single training process.
The framework uses a Progress State Encoder to construct a shared state embedding from route context, historical segment-level travel-time histograms, and attention-based sequence modeling.

The framework combines a Segment Travel Time Estimator using local spatio-temporal graphs and a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with a Next Segment Prediction module using multi-hop look-ahead neighborhoods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on large-scale real-world datasets are reported to show that UNITE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Travel time estimation on road networks is important for location-based services and has origin-destination and route variants.
Existing approaches generally treat the two estimation variants separately.
UNITE addresses both variants through a single progressive, segment-wise training framework with a shared state representation.
The framework estimates segment travel times with spatio-temporal graphs and Mixture-of-Experts modeling, while predicting next segments using multi-hop neighborhoods.
The authors report improved accuracy and efficiency over state-of-the-art methods on large-scale real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses one shared state embedding and one training process for two related travel-time estimation variants.

interpretation.claim: A shared representation may reduce duplicated modeling across closely related prediction tasks.

application.claim: For systems with related estimation tasks, consider a common context representation when the tasks share sequential and dynamic conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when a unified model is preferable to separate task-specific models.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the state-of-the-art baselines or experimental settings.
